## Paper

Cooperation and Contagion in Web-Based, Networked Public Goods Experiments

## World

public_goods

## Institution

Information restriction / networked observability.

## Agent type

Public-goods participants under limited or networked information.

## Theoretical benchmark

Network structure and observability affect cooperation contagion and contribution dynamics.

## Learning setup

Repeated public-goods game where observations restrict or expose social information.

## Metrics

Contribution, sustainability, welfare, information-condition deltas, variance across seeds.

## Main result

Network topology had no significant effect on average contributions; positive effects of cooperation were contagious only to direct neighbors

## What they prove

Network topology had no significant effect on average contributions; positive effects of cooperation were contagious only to direct neighbors

## What they only simulate

The effect of seed players on contributions; contagion effects

## What they do NOT test

The effect of different levels of positive/negative influence at different distances from human players

## What we need to reproduce

Treat information restrictions as strategic observability changes and report whether contribution/sustainability differs from baseline.

## How our project differs

The paper studies networked human experiments. The repo implements a simple information restriction, not a full social network.

## Implementation obligations

Observation transform; baseline comparison; contribution/sustainability deltas; note absence of explicit network topology unless added.

## Metrics to compare in our repo

information_restriction institution and contribution/sustainability deltas in Public Goods outputs.

## Failure modes to audit

Calling an observation mask a network experiment; no state metric movement; no variance/seed reporting.

Compare Cooperation and Contagion in Web-Based, Networked Public Goods Experiments to information_restriction Public Goods outputs. The repo can use it as an observability anchor with a clear simplification caveat.
